name: Gambian Domoda
description: Domoda, Gambia's national dish, is genuinely built on real sweet potato or pumpkin as a core vegetable, not just meat, tomato, and peanut alone - when meat isn't used, the vegetable itself carries much of the dish. Real technique fries the aromatics and tomato paste down first, then simmers everything until the oil visibly rises to the surface, the same real doneness cue found in neighboring Sudanese cooking.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the onion and garlic, 8-9 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the diced tomatoes and jalapeño, add to the pot along with the sweet potato and 1 cup water.
Simmer 30-35 minutes, until the sweet potato is tender and the oil visibly rises to the surface - the real sign the stew is done.

name: Gambian Benachin
description: Benachin, meaning 'one pot' in Wolof, is one of Gambia's most iconic dishes - real technique fries the chicken first, sets it aside, builds the tomato base in the same pot, then returns everything together with the rice so the flavors genuinely meld as one.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Rice, white, long-grain, parboiled, enriched, dry

ingredients.ingredient: Rice, white, long-grain, parboiled, enriched, dry

steps_detailed: Brown the chicken, 6-7 minutes, then set aside.
Fry the onion in the same pot, add the tomato paste, cook 2 minutes, then add the diced tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the carrot and cabbage, and simmer 8-10 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the rice and broth, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes until the rice is tender.

name: Gambian Superkanja
description: Superkanja, a hearty okra stew, is a beloved Gambian dish, thickened naturally by real okra's own sliminess.
steps_detailed: Cook the tomatoes in the palm oil, 5-6 minutes.
Add the fish and okra with a splash of water, and simmer 12-15 minutes until the fish is cooked through and the stew thickens naturally.

name: Gambian Chicken Yassa
description: Chicken yassa, marinated and slow-cooked in caramelized onions and lemon, is a beloved Gambian street food, real technique cooking the onions down until genuinely sweet, not just softened.
steps_detailed: Marinate the chicken in the lemon juice, mustard, and garlic for at least 20 minutes.
Brown the chicken in a little oil, 6-7 minutes, then set aside.
Cook the onion over medium-low heat, stirring often, 20-25 minutes, until deeply softened and sweet.
Return the chicken with a splash of water and simmer 15 minutes more.

name: Gambian Afra
description: Afra, barbecued meat, is a beloved Gambian street food, real technique keeping the seasoning simple so the smoky char carries the flavor.
steps_detailed: Rub the beef with the garlic and pepper.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 12-15 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.

description: Bissap, a hibiscus drink, is a beloved Gambian beverage shared across much of West Africa.
steps_detailed: Warm the hibiscus tea and stir in the sugar until dissolved.
Chill and serve over ice.

name: Gambian Peanut Sauce
description: A simple ground-peanut sauce base, echoing the flavor of domoda, used across many Gambian stews.

Simmer 12-15 minutes until thickened.
